cases.statement: One person: P11 of a 112-patient adult-onset spasticity cohort screened with a leukodystrophy panel; male, onset at 70. Table-only description.

people.label: P11
people.key_phenotypes: spastic paraplegia (cohort inclusion); onset at 70; ataxia; urinary retention; oblongata-to-cervical atrophy on MRI

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: oblongata-to-cervical atrophy, ataxia and urinary retention (Table 2). Cohort-level: patients were screened negative for SPG4 and SPG11 and for acquired causes, then tested with a 130-gene leukoencephalopathy panel; the authors say AxD patients were diagnosed on the medulla-to-cervical atrophy pattern.

quotes.quote: (4) no causative genes were found during the gene screening for SPG4 and SPG 11, which are the most common types of HSP.
Firstly, a custom-designed probe library containing 130 known pathogenic genes reported to be associated with hereditary leukoencephalopathies was synthesized (Supplementary Table 1).

Each patient was eventually diagnosed based on the characteristic MRI findings of severe atrophy from the medulla oblongata to the upper cervical cord; of note, the extensive cerebral white matter abnormalities often observed in infantile and juvenile cases were not common in our patients.

segregation.statement: No segregation data reported for P11; Table 2 marks no affected siblings. Methods say segregation was done only when relatives' DNA was available (cohort-level).

quotes.quote: Segregation tests were performed if the DNA of the proband’s immediate family member was available, and the final pathogenic mutations were determined in combination with the clinical information.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Glu206Lys). The paper makes no mechanism statement for GFAP.

computational_predictions.statement: SIFT damaging; Mutation Taster damaging; PolyPhen2 probably damaging (no scores given).

authors_classification.statement: Table 1 gives the authors' ACMG call for this variant (no criteria codes); the Results text nevertheless counts the three AxD patients among the 13 with identified disease-causing mutations.

quotes.quote: | P11 | GFAP | c.616G>A | p.E206K | No | VUS | Damaging | Damaging | Probably damaging |

We identified pathogenic mutations in 13 of the 112 patients, including five patients with adrenomyeloneuropathy (AMN), three with KD, three with Alexander disease (AxD), and two with cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX).

concerns: The paper contradicts itself: Table 1 gives an intermediate ACMG tier for c.616G>A (see authors_classification), while the Results count P11 among patients with identified disease-causing mutations and assign the diagnosis AxD.
The Discussion says 'Neither case in our series had palatal myoclonus or prominent ataxia', implying two AxD cases, although Table 2 lists three AxD patients and marks ataxia '+' for P11.
Table-only description: no case narrative for P11 (only P9 is described); zygosity and transcript not stated.
notes_for_panel: Late-onset case from a Chinese HSP-mimic cohort, with imaging typical of adult-onset AxD per the authors and three in-silico predictions. No segregation, de novo, functional or population data.
